One-sided spectrum of a column.

The one-sided spectrum of one numeric column as a new table of n / 2 + 1 rows: frequency, period, amplitude (2 |X| / sum of the window, the amplitude of a tone), phase, power density (scipy periodogram), real and imag (numpy.fft.rfft of the windowed, mean-removed signal). A branch for looking at a signal: the row count changes, so training does not read it.

## Settings

| Setting | Key | Type | Default | Allowed values | Read by | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| signal_col | `signal_col` | Text | (empty) |   | The run | Numeric signal column. Required. |
| sample_rate | `sample_rate` | Number | `1.0` | `> 0` | The run | Samples per second (per unit, per row) for the frequency axis. |
| window | `window` | Choice | `hann` | `hann`, `hamming`, `blackman`, `boxcar` | The run | The window applied first (periodic, as scipy.signal.get_window) |
| remove_mean | `remove_mean` | On / off | `true` |   | The run | Take the mean out before the transform. |
| remove_trend | `remove_trend` | On / off | `false` |   | The run | Take a least-squares line out first (a trending signal otherwise puts its whole length on top) |

**Read by** says whether a run uses the setting (**The run**) or only the editor, a dialog or a view (**The editor only**).
